raw_response:
Looking at my situation: I've been farming this land for over 30 years, and my family's land is about 10 mu total in Quzhou. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat then summer corn — it's the rotation I know, the buyers are reliable, and the input costs are predictable. My neighbors do it, my father did it, and the village cooperative helps us sell both.

I'm not going to try cotton — prices have been bad and it needs too much hand labor my back can't handle anymore. I've heard about people trying vegetables but that's risky without a contract, and I don't have connections to those markets.

For wheat this coming winter, I'll plant improved seed (the agricultural station here pushed "Jimai 22" and it outyields the traditional seed we used to save). For corn in summer, I've been using hybrid seed for years — no question there. I use rotary tillage before wheat because my fields get compacted; for corn I just go straight in after wheat harvest since time is tight.

On fertilizer, I put down a bit more than recommended — the soil here is thin and I'd rather not risk a bad yield. My irrigation schedule follows what I've always done: wheat needs water 3-4 times (jointing, heading, grain fill, and one in winter), corn only needs 1-2 since summer rains usually help.

For pesticide, wheat gets sprayed for rust and aphids in spring — can't skip that. Corn gets one herbicide pass early on.

Wheat receives four irrigations to cover the water-deficit growing season; maize relies more on summer rainfall with two supplemental irrigations.
